title: Roundabouts
whatItIs: A junction where traffic goes round a central island. Give priority to traffic approaching from your right, unless signs, markings or lights say otherwise.
keyFacts: Use Mirrors – Signal – Manoeuvre at every stage and decide on your exit early.
Give way to traffic from your right, unless signs, road markings or traffic lights say otherwise.
Follow lane markings. Where there are none, pick the lane that suits your exit.

keyFacts.text: At a mini-roundabout you MUST go round the central marking (except large vehicles that can't).

keyFacts: At double or multiple roundabouts, treat each one separately.
Watch for cyclists, motorcyclists, horse riders and long vehicles on the roundabout.

visual.caption: Lanes and signals at a four-way roundabout

routes.label: 1st exit · turning left
steps: Signal left and approach in the left lane
Keep to the left and keep signalling left

routes.label: 2nd exit · going ahead
steps: Choose the appropriate lane; usually no signal on approach
Signal left after passing the 1st exit

routes.label: 3rd exit · turning right
steps: Signal right and approach in the right lane
Keep to the right on the roundabout
Signal left after passing the 2nd exit

a.label: Roundabout
points: Warning sign: triangle with arrows going round

b.label: Mini-roundabout
points: White central circle marked on the road
Blue circular sign with three white arrows
Less space and time: avoid U-turns

onTheTest.question: You're going straight ahead at a roundabout (2nd exit). When should you signal left?
options: After passing the exit before the one you want
Only if there is traffic behind you
onTheTest.why: Going ahead, you don't normally signal on approach. Signal left once you've passed the exit before yours.

onTheTest.question: A cyclist on the roundabout is in the left lane and signalling right. What should you do?
options: Sound your horn to warn them
Overtake them quickly on the right
Assume they'll take the next exit
onTheTest.why: Cyclists and horse riders may stay in the left lane and signal right if they're going round. Give them space and let them cross your path.

traps: Going ahead? Don't signal left on approach: signal left only after passing the exit before yours.
A cyclist or horse rider in the left lane may be going all the way round.
Long vehicles may need more than one lane: hang back and watch their signals.
